name: epiq
desc:
Legal Contact Center Agent | $16-$20/hr | Phone Heavy, No Sales Expectations
Company: Epiq
Industry: Customer Service
What Your Day Will Look Like: In plain terms: you are not solving deep legal problems or making legal decisions. You are the first point of contact who explains what the notice means, walks people through the basic process, answers routine questions, and hands off anything complex. The job is high-volume customer service inside a legal administration environment.

handle a steady stream of interactions from people who have received legal notices. Typical callers include:
Class members or claimants asking “Did I get the settlement notice? How do I file a claim? When will I get paid? Why was my claim rejected?”
People who received a data breach notification letter and are worried, confused, or want help enrolling in free credit monitoring / identity protection
Creditors or parties in a bankruptcy case checking status or submitting information
Occasionally attorneys or other parties needing basic case information

Your core work looks like this:
Answer inbound calls, emails, chats, and callbacks professionally.
Follow approved scripts and FAQs to give consistent, accurate information.
Verify the caller’s identity when required.
Guide people through simple next steps (how to submit a claim, how to register for credit monitoring, how to check status online, etc.).
Make outbound calls when something needs follow-up or is escalated.
When the issue is more complicated than the script allows, document it clearly and escalate it to the internal research team.
Stay calm and professional with frustrated, angry, or anxious callers (common when people feel they are owed money or their personal data was exposed).
Log every interaction accurately in the system.
Stick tightly to your assigned schedule and call-flow rules.
Submit your time entries correctly (Epiq bills clients for this work, so time tracking matters).
assessment: Yes, expect an assessment after applying or after initial contact with recruiter. Expect typing, grammar, behavioral, and internet speed assessments.
skills:
Actual Minimum Requirements
Education Minimum: High school diploma or equivalent.
Required Experience: Customer service or similar experience. No number of years is listed.
Preferred Experience: Call center experience.
Required Skills:
• Professional phone manner, including on difficult calls
• Ability to follow an assigned schedule and call flow
• Comfort handling calls, email, chat, and callbacks
• Good judgment about when to pass a complex issue to the research team
• Accurate time entry for billing and payroll
• Ability to sit, stand, and use standard office equipment
Best Fit
This role is ideal for:
• Someone with some customer service experience who wants to get into a legal services company
• Someone calm and professional with upset callers
• Someone who follows a call flow and an assigned schedule well
• Someone comfortable switching between calls, email, and chat
Not a Good Fit for:
• Anyone who dislikes being on the phone most of the day
• Anyone who needs to set their own schedule, since the posting says you follow an assigned schedule
• Anyone who gets stressed by escalated or difficult calls
notes:
Expected Application & Interviewing Process: 1. Application 2. Expect an assessment at the end of the application or directly emailed to you. 3. If assessment is passing, expect a recruiter to reach out via email or text for a phone screen. 4. If phone screen passes you can expect the final interview. Total time to hire from date of application can be anywhere from 3-15 days on average.
Top 10 Resume Keywords:
• Inbound and outbound call handling
• Customer service
• Call center experience
• Email, chat, and callback support
• Escalation handling
• De-escalation on difficult calls
• Following call flows and schedules
• Accurate time and record entry
• Professional communication
• Legal or professional services support
4-5 interview questions for this role:
• Tell us about your customer service or call center experience.
• How do you stay calm and professional when a caller is upset?
• How do you decide when to pass a complex issue to someone else?
• How do you stay on track following a call flow and an assigned schedule?
• How do you keep your time and records accurate when you’re busy?
other:
Pay, Shift, Benefits, Background, Drug Test Information, and Career Pathway:

Pay: Not stated in posting. Estimated $16 to $20/hr based on third party estimates for Epiq contact center roles, not confirmed by Epiq. Confirm directly.

Shift: Not stated in posting. You follow an assigned schedule. The posting shows both part-time and full-time, so confirm the hours directly.

Benefits: Not itemized in posting. Epiq lists its benefits on a separate page, so confirm directly.

Equipment Provided: Not stated in posting.

Felony Friendly?: Case by case.

Drug Test: Certain positions.

Notes: This is a good way into the legal services industry from a call center or customer service job. Epiq says it will consider qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records where the law allows. The posting lists Houston, TX as the location for this remote job, so confirm where Epiq hires.

Career Pathway: Reasonable inferred path: Contact Center Agent → Senior Agent → Team Lead → Contact Center Supervisor.
training: Discussed in interview/offer stage. Must be available for any shift.
